scope: Night-3B P22 FULL_IGE seeds 0-4 historical B00 numerical reuse only
required_preflight_checks: All five official run_manifest.json files identify dataset p22, variant FULL_IGE and the matching seed.
Every required artifact exists and its recomputed SHA-256 equals run_manifest.artifact_sha256.
Every checkpoint_index.csv has exactly 10 registered rows and state_file_saved=False for every row.
The last checkpoint row is step 1600 and its state_sha256 equals run_manifest.final_state_sha256.
Manifest initial_state_sha256 and final_state_sha256 are present and valid 64-character lowercase SHA-256 strings.
The run manifest and artifacts are covered by the official Night-3B delivery inventory/SHA protection.
Current code can reconstruct the matching initial state and initial no-label probe from the locked seed, code and immutable cache; this check must not retrain or overwrite the historical run.

After the Night-5D total training/transform lock and label-window opening, historical clusters/embeddings are re-evaluated and seeds 0-4 metrics match the locked Night-3B metrics within the taskbook tolerance.
explicitly_forbidden: Treating the absent model-state file as if it had been verified.
Substituting any Night-3AF model_final.pt for a Night-3B FULL_IGE state.
Reconstructing or fabricating a checkpoint file from a recorded state hash.
Rerunning Night-3B B00 seeds 0-4 to replace the historical numerical baseline.
Claiming historical final weights are reloadable or available for checkpoint-level analysis.
permitted_scientific_use: Reuse the SHA-verified historical embedding and clusters as B00 numerical baseline for seeds 0-4.
Recompute ARI, NMI, Q and spatial metrics from the verified outputs after the label firewall opens.
Pair each historical B00 seed 0-4 metric with the same Night-5D candidate seed in preregistered statistics.
scientific_limitation: The historical B00 outputs are auditable numerical result artifacts, but their final model weights were intentionally not delivered and cannot support final-weight reload, checkpoint perturbation, or weight-level reproducibility claims.
